newsitem.title: UK: Yorks Electricity aims to grow, up benefits.
newsitem.headline: Yorks Electricity aims to grow, up benefits.

text.p: British electricity generator Yorkshire Electricity Group Plc said on Tuesday it could grow supply and generation businesses while returning value to shareholders despite recent tax changes.
Yorkshire highlighted recent changes to capital allowances by finance minister Kenneth Clarke and the opposition Labour party's proposed plans for a one-off windfall tax on utilities.

But despite these, it said: "We have the financial capability to grow our competitive energy supply and generation businesses and to return further value to shareholders, and we intend to do both," the company said in a statement.

Yorkshire said it expected a higher contribution from its distribution business in the second half than in the first while the supply business would have a lower profit, reflecting the shape of each unit's revenues and costs.
Yorkshire turned in pretax profits for the six months ending September 30 of 80.8 million stg, down from 110.6 million stg previously as a pricing review earlier this year took effect.
It paid out an interim dividend of 15.8 pence per share, a jump of 33 percent from a year ago.

Yorkshire said it was confident of remaining competitive as an independent regional electricity company (Rec) despite current restructuring in the industry which has left it one of only three remaining independent and unpursued.
It said it was concerned over costs of implementing the competitive market, scheduled for 1998, but welcomed recent proposals to phase in competition.
"It remains our strategy to be highly competitive in our core energy businesses whilst continuing to provide value for all of our stakeholders," chairman Christopher Hampson said in a statement.
